:::{#exm-induced-norm}
#### The norm induced by the dot product

In $\reals^p$ [equipped with](#def-inner-product-space) the [dot product](#def-dot-product) (@exm-inner-product-space),
@eq-induced-norm gives $\norm{\vx} = \sqrt{\vx \cdot \vx}$.
By @thm-norm-dot-product,
this [induced norm](#def-induced-norm) is the same as the [Euclidean norm](#def-euclidean-norm).
For $\vx = (3, 4)$:

$$
\ba
\sqrt{\vx \cdot \vx}
&= \sqrt{3 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 4}
&& \text{(@eq-inner-product)}
\\
&= \sqrt{25}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 5
\ea
$$

which is the [length](#def-euclidean-norm) that @exm-euclidean-norm found.

Every inner product space $(\reals^p, \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot})$ (@def-inner-product-space)
has an induced norm,
which satisfies all three axioms of a [norm](#def-norm).

<!-- no-figure: the example computes one number, for the vector that @exm-euclidean-norm already uses -->

:::
